failed_attempts.failure_reason: Vast.ai create-instance API responded with empty stdout/exit 0 for the first call but created a duplicate instance shortly afterwards (37106446); both 37106446 and 37106453 were created from the same offer ID. 37106446 was destroyed via the API (returned 404 'Instance not found' on destroy probe -- it was already removed Vast.ai-side, likely a transient phantom from the create-instance race).

SSH authentication rejected the registered key (id 801863 with comment 'shefuniad\md1avn@TEN00BE4360B45A'). After 5 retries on ssh4.vast.ai:26452 (proxy) and one attempt on 76.64.86.119:47399 (direct), all 6 returned 'Permission denied (publickey)' despite the key being attached to the instance per Vast.ai API. Root cause: the literal backslash in the key comment field appears to corrupt key parsing in the Vast.ai SSH proxy (the key was stored with double-escaped backslash 'shefuniad\\md1avn'). Resolution: registered a new SSH key entry (id 855344) using the same key material but a clean ASCII comment 'md1avn-t0113', attached to the next instance, and SSH connected successfully on the first attempt.

mod_compile.note_on_load_mechanisms: Modern NEURON places libnrnmech.so directly in x86_64/ (not in x86_64/.libs/ as older versions did). 'load_mechanisms(x86_64)' from Python returns False because it looks for the legacy path, but hasattr(h, 'bkt80') etc. all return True because NEURON auto-loads x86_64/libnrnmech.so from CWD on import. This matches t0112's observation exactly.
